clue.text: Servant attending gentleman before a dance

blocks.note: a valet is a manservant who looks after a gentleman's clothes and needs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentleman's manservant is fussing over him just before they head off to a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole first half reads as one long description of the servant, leaving only the last word to define.
explanation.definitionFit: The valeta is an old-time ballroom sequence routine in waltz time, popular in British halls.

clue.text: Animation in shout from some Manchester supporters?

blocks.note: first meaning: liveliness, high spirits
second meaning, punning: fans of Manchester City might cry 'Long live City!' in Italian-style cheering

explanation.surface: A lively chant goes up from part of a Manchester football crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as VIVA CITY: 'viva' is the cheer 'long live', and City is Manchester City, one of the city's two big football clubs; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivacity is liveliness or spirited energy, which is what animation means when describing a person.

clue.text: Alternative to match that's comparatively easy to shift

blocks.note: first meaning: a device for producing a flame, used instead of a match
second meaning: weighing less than something else, so easier to move

explanation.surface: Something offered instead of a match turns out simpler to move around.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flame-making gadget used in place of a match, and lighter is also the comparative of the adjective meaning low in weight.

clue.text: Open-mindedness from an elector, unusually

indicators.note: doing something unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters are put in an abnormal order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A voter is surprisingly broad-minded, which is not what you would expect from them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is the willingness to accept views and behaviour different from your own, the essence of being open-minded.

clue.text: Song for church service

blocks.note: an air is a tune or song
taken as written
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone is choosing a hymn for a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church service' reads as one phrase, but the split falls between them: church supplies letters and service alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The air force is one of the armed services, alongside the army and navy.

clue.text: In visionary way, decide a list I call, yet not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only a part of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters inside them

blocks.clueFragment: decide a list I call, yet
blocks.note: the letters run from inside the first word to the first letter of the last

explanation.surface: Someone reads out a wish list in a dreamy manner while deciding, though not quite finishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run is unusually long, spanning five words and needing only the first two letters of 'decide' and the first of 'yet' dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealistically means in a way guided by ideals rather than practicality, which is how a visionary behaves.

clue.text: Half-heartedly attacked person with convictions

indicators.note: doing something half-heartedly loses half of its heart, so one of the two central letters is dropped

blocks.note: fell on means attacked, as in to fall on an enemy

explanation.surface: Someone launches a feeble attack on a person of strong principles.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of FELL ON is the double L; losing half of it leaves one L.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is a criminal, someone found guilty in court, playing on convictions as beliefs versus verdicts.

clue.text: Lie about Conservative policy

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a party line is its policy

explanation.surface: An accusation that someone is lying about Tory policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie about' suggests deceit and a container, but lie is the verb meaning lean back, and about is just RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lie back or lean in a relaxed position, so it can replace lie as a verb.

clue.text: What could be green before end of century?

definitions.text: What could be green before end of century?

indicators.note: could be suggests what the following letters might become if they were rearranged
end of points to the very last letter of the following word

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A question about what might become environmentally friendly before the century is out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: green power from wind and sun is the goal many countries set for the end of this century.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy is the power supply that campaigners want to become renewable, the commonest thing called green in that sense.

clue.text: Finally attributed blame to sinner wrongly — it's not provable

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it qualifies
wrongly means not in the right way, so these letters are set in an incorrect order

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eventually pins the fault on a wrongdoer, though it can't be proved.
explanation.walkthrough: Fourteen letters of fodder: the D plus all of 'blame to sinner' mix into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indemonstrable cannot be shown or established as true, so it is incapable of being proved.

clue.text: Member of unofficial force leaving it after order's changed

indicators.note: once the order is changed the letters no longer stand in their original sequence

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Someone quits an unauthorised militia after its orders are altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' sounds like a command given to the force, but it refers to the sequence of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante is a self-appointed enforcer who takes the law into their own hands without legal authority.

clue.text: Something you might pick by European or English philosopher

blocks.note: a burglar can pick a lock
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Choosing between a continental thinker and an English one.
explanation.walkthrough: John Locke was a 17th-century English philosopher of empiricism and liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke is a famous English thinker, so the answer is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Resting-place beside lake for exclusive group

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
Lake Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A lakeside retreat set aside for a select clique.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small, select circle of people with shared interests who tend to keep others out.

clue.text: Advancing conclusion after conclusion in trial

indicators.note: the conclusion in a word is its final letter

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
an ending is a conclusion

explanation.surface: A court case is moving towards one verdict after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word does two jobs: the first conclusion is a synonym, the second picks the last letter of trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Lending is advancing money, as in advancing someone a loan.

clue.text: Act to capture one of the Romans elsewhere in Italy

indicators.note: to capture something is to take it inside, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: a turn is an act or routine in a variety show
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A performance about seizing a Roman, set somewhere else in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of the Romans' looks like a person, but it means the Roman numeral for one. 'Elsewhere' says the city is in Italy but is not Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in northern Italy, an Italian location other than the Rome the Romans suggest.

clue.text: Old boy was in the army, it's said

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a soldier is said to have served

explanation.surface: Word has it that a former pupil did military service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' sounds like a sound-alike signal, but there is none: said is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Observed in the sense of remarked or commented is a synonym of said.

clue.text: Put back in control, play for time

blocks.note: to rein in is to control, and reins are a means of control
to stall is to delay deliberately

explanation.surface: Someone restored to power stalls to buy time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back in control' reads as one phrase about restoring a leader; the definition stops at back.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstall something is to install it again, putting it back in its place.

clue.text: Repairman set out in error, confused

indicators.note: out here means put out of place, so the letters are disturbed
confused means jumbled up, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled mechanic heads off on a job by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorer is someone who repairs old furniture, paintings or buildings to their former condition.

clue.text: Party activity for people who've gone downhill fast

definitions.text: Party activity for people who've gone downhill fast

blocks.note: surface reading: people whose fortunes or health have declined rapidly
setter's reading: the socialising skiers enjoy once a day of racing down the slopes is over

explanation.surface: A party thrown for people in steep decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone downhill fast' is an idiom for deteriorating, but here it is literal: skiers have sped down a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is French for after skiing and names the evening socialising at a ski resort.

clue.text: Dashing manner of pirate's enemy enduring pain

blocks.note: Peter Pan is the enemy of the pirate Captain Hook
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A swashbuckling style belongs to the pirate's foe, who puts up with pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant confidence and style, a dashing flair.

clue.text: Children matter

blocks.note: first meaning: offspring, a legal term for descendants
second meaning: a topic or point for discussion

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a slogan that kids are important; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal word for offspring, and also a subject or point under debate.

clue.text: Pupil's education briefly held up by daring feat

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
something held is gripped inside something else

blocks.note: ED is the short form of education
a stunt is a daring feat

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's learning is interrupted by a dangerous stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A student is someone learning at a school or university, which is what a pupil is.

clue.text: Bloke almost rented holiday accommodation

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a chap is a man
a property is let when it is rented out

explanation.surface: A man has nearly rented somewhere to stay on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cabin, often in a ski resort or holiday camp, rented by holidaymakers.

clue.text: Result of overindulgence less good for royal house

indicators.note: less means minus, so something is taken away

blocks.note: the after-effect of drinking too much
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Excess is bad for a royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Hanover ruled Britain from George I in 1714 to Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanover is the German dynasty that held the British throne in the 18th and 19th centuries.

clue.text: Superior middle-class house in very bad area

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
ill means bad, as in ill effects
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A posh suburban home sits in a rough part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but it only joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a villa is a detached suburban house of some pretension, typical of the comfortable middle classes.

clue.text: Like sailor, we hear, in storm

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

blocks.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor, so like a sailor is as salt

explanation.surface: Someone behaves like a seaman in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' sounds like weather at sea, but it is the military sense of an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a place is to attack it forcefully, so storm and assault are synonyms as nouns or verbs.

clue.text: A high-ranking officer turned left — not general

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
COL is the abbreviation for colonel
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A senior officer veered left, though he was not a general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army rank beside the officer, but it means widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: Local means confined to a particular area, the opposite of widespread or general.

clue.text: Singer getting a buck, perhaps, after dance

indicators.note: after says the piece just named comes later in the answer than the word that follows it

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance
taken as written
a buck is a male deer, so a deer by example

explanation.surface: A vocalist is paid a dollar once the dance is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' suggests a dollar, but 'perhaps' marks it as an example of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A balladeer is a singer of ballads, narrative or sentimental songs.

clue.text: Generate reforms in youth

indicators.note: reforms means forms again in a new shape, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A call to bring about change among young people.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, and a teenager is someone aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Province historically included in consul's territory

indicators.note: included in means sitting inside, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A former province lay within a Roman consul's lands.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is one of Ireland's four historic provinces; its name is now often used loosely for Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is one of the four ancient provinces of Ireland, so it is a province in the historical sense.
